claims.text: Cold rolling increases dislocation density in magnetic high-entropy alloys.
Increased dislocation density enhances magnetic domain-wall pinning.
Enhanced domain-wall pinning increases the coercive field of magnetic high-entropy alloys.
The as-cast or annealed baseline alloy has a relatively low dislocation density.
Controlled cold rolling introduces a higher density of dislocations into the alloy.
Cold rolling can be conducted within a deformation range that avoids phase transformations and excessive grain refinement.
Dislocations and related microstructural defects act as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
Additional pinning sites obstruct domain-wall motion and require a higher applied field to reverse magnetization.
Cold-rolled samples will have a statistically significant increase in coercive field relative to annealed baseline samples.
Phase transformations or excessive grain-boundary modifications may counteract dislocation-related domain-wall pinning.
Domain-wall pinning by dislocations is well documented in conventional magnetic materials.
Complex high-entropy-alloy microstructures might alter the effectiveness of dislocation-related pinning.
Failure of cold-rolled samples to show a statistically significant coercivity increase, or observation of reduced coercivity, would falsify the hypothesis.
